tldr: OpenAI engineers spent months chasing mysterious crashes in Rockset, the C++ data infrastructure behind ChatGPT search, where functions returned to invalid addresses and stack pointers shifted unexpectedly. Instead of debugging crashes one at a time, they built a pipeline to mine a year of production core dumps for population-level patterns — "epidemiological debugging."
whats_new: InfoQ's write-up details the fix: an 18-year-old GNU libunwind race condition with a roughly 100-picosecond vulnerable window, made real by OpenAI's frequent per-query timer signals, has been patched upstream by reordering the instruction- and stack-pointer updates.
why_it_matters: A textbook 18-year-old unwinding-library race only became visible at OpenAI's request volume and signal frequency — a reminder that widely-used systems libraries can hide production-breaking bugs that only trigger at extreme scale or aggressive timer/signal usage.

status.detail: Root-caused to a silent Azure hardware fault plus an upstream libunwind race condition; the software fix has been submitted upstream.

beats.headline: OpenAI mines a year of ChatGPT core dumps to catch untraceable Rockset crashes
beats.summary: An automated core-dump pipeline replaced one-crash-at-a-time debugging with population-level pattern search across return-to-null and misaligned-stack failures.

beats.headline: Root cause: a silent Azure hardware fault plus an 18-year-old libunwind race condition
beats.summary: The software bug's vulnerable window was about 100 picoseconds — only exposed by OpenAI's frequent per-query timer signals — and was closed by reordering the pointer updates.

open_questions: Has the libunwind race-condition fix landed in a released version, or only been submitted upstream?
Did the same Azure hardware fault affect other tenants on that host, or was it isolated to OpenAI's workload?
take_for_builders: If your service delivers signals frequently (per-query timers, profilers) on a C/C++ stack that links libunwind for exception unwinding, check whether your build already carries the upstream setcontext fix before writing off 'impossible' crashes as hardware noise.
